newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

The Bank of Indonesia announced an expansion of the intervention band to eight percent and a rise in the minimum reserve requirement to five percent on Wednesday to stabilise the money supply and cool down the economy. Inflation is still higher than the government target of five percent.

The United States said on Wednesday that member countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) could not expect to receive aid indefinitely and that trade and investment should be the main engine for development in the region. The United States was meeting its dialogue partners from the ASEAN countries on Batam Island in what is an annual forum to discuss matters of mutual concern.
The list of candidates for the official government party Golkar could still be changed before next Monday's deadline, party chairman Harmoko said. Parliamentary elections are scheduled for 1997.

Over 50 percent of Japanese businessmen operating in Indonesia find bureauracy the worst problem, a survey published on Wednesday said. The survey of Japenese manufacturers across ASEAN countries did not find bureaucracy a problem outside Indonesia.
